Thriller.text: It spent a record 37 non-consecutive weeks at number one on the Billboard album chart.
Thriller.evidence: Thriller was Jackson's first number-one album on the Billboard Top LPs & Tape chart and was at number one for a record 37 non-consecutive weeks.

Back in Black.text: The all-black cover was designed as a "sign of mourning" for the band's late singer Bon Scott.
Back in Black.evidence: The album's all-black cover was designed as a "sign of mourning" for Scott.

The Bodyguard.text: In its sixth week it sold a million copies in a single week, a first verified by Nielsen SoundScan.
The Bodyguard.evidence: In its sixth week, it sold one million copies within a single week, making Houston the first artist to accomplish this following verification by Nielsen SoundScan.

The Dark Side of the Moon.text: It has spent 996 weeks on the US Billboard album chart.
The Dark Side of the Moon.evidence: The Dark Side of the Moon is certified 14× platinum in the United Kingdom, and topped the US Billboard Top LPs & Tape chart, where it has charted for 996 weeks.

Their Greatest Hits.text: The first album ever to receive an RIAA Platinum certification, which was introduced in 1976.
Their Greatest Hits.evidence: The album has the distinction of being the first album to receive a Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) Platinum certification, which was introduced in 1976 to recognize albums that ship at least one million copies in the United States.

Hotel California.text: The cover is a photograph of the Beverly Hills Hotel.
Hotel California.evidence: The album cover is a photograph of the Beverly Hills Hotel, taken by David Alexander.

Come On Over.text: The best-selling studio album by a woman, and the best-selling country album.
Come On Over.evidence: Come On Over is the best-selling studio album by a woman, the best-selling country album, and one of the best-selling albums of all time, having sold over 40 million copies worldwide.

Rumours.text: It was recorded while the band members dealt with breakups with one another and heavy drug use.
Rumours.evidence: The recording sessions took place as the band members dealt with breakups with one another and struggled with heavy drug use, both of which shaped the album's direction and lyrics.

Bat Out of Hell.text: It grew out of Neverland, Jim Steinman's futuristic rock version of Peter Pan.
Bat Out of Hell.evidence: Composed by Jim Steinman, the album was developed from the musical Neverland, a futuristic rock version of Peter Pan which Steinman wrote for a workshop in 1974.

Saturday Night Fever.text: The Bee Gees wrote their songs for it "virtually in a single weekend" at a studio in France.
Saturday Night Fever.evidence: The brothers wrote the songs "virtually in a single weekend" at Château d'Hérouville studio in France.
